subject: zoology
question_text: Mention the animals that exhibited a 'tube-within-a-tube' organisation for the first time. Name their body cavity.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.51, VSAQ 74). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Animals that show it first
steps.why: The phrase names the plan itself, so the answer names the phylum and then says which structure is each of the two tubes.
common_mistakes: Naming Platyhelminthes. Flatworms have an incomplete gut with no anus, so no inner tube runs right through the body.
Naming Annelida. The plan appears earlier, in Nematoda.
steps.memory_tip: Two tubes: the body wall outside, the gut from mouth to anus inside.
steps.margin_note: Name the phylum, then say which structure is each tube. Two short lines.
lines: The 'tube-within-a-tube' plan is seen for the
first time in the phylum Nematoda
The body wall is the outer tube and the
alimentary canal is the inner tube.

steps.label: Their body cavity
steps.why: Nematodes keep the embryonic blastocoel as their body cavity, and because it has no complete mesodermal lining it is called a false coelom.
common_mistakes: Calling it a true coelom. A true coelom is lined by mesoderm on both sides; the nematode cavity is not.
steps.memory_tip: Pseudo means false: the cavity is there, the complete mesodermal lining is not.
steps.margin_note: One word carries this mark — pseudocoelom. Add one line saying why it is called false.
